source_document.title: Starting Strength: Basic Barbell Training - Chapter 2: The Squat
source_document.author: Mark Rippetoe

criteria.name: Squat Depth (Below Parallel)
criteria.paraphrased_rule: The apex of the crease of the shorts (Point B) must drop clearly below the top of the patella (Point A) so the femoral plane breaks parallel with the floor.
criteria.metric_definition: Vertical Y position of hip joint crease relative to the superior border of the patella at the lowest turnaround frame (y_hip > y_patella in downward-positive image coordinates).
criteria.pass_condition_document: Hip crease drops below the top of the patella at bottom inflection.

app_tolerance.description: ASSUMPTION: Hip joint keypoint is an anatomical proxy for crease apex B; margins between -0.8cm and +0.8cm are flagged as borderline uncertain.

feedback_messages.meets_standard: Depth meets standard: Hip crease dropped below the top of the patella (below parallel). Satisfies Starting Strength full range of motion, balancing anterior-posterior knee forces.
feedback_messages.does_not_meet_standard: Squat was high (above parallel). The hip crease remained above the top of the patella. As stated on Ref p. 15, partial squats predominantly stress the quadriceps and patellar tendon without recruiting the posterior chain. Check stance width and shove knees out to reach full depth.
feedback_messages.cannot_assess: Squat depth cannot be assessed: hip crease or patella landmarks are occluded, framing is cut off, or camera is non-sagittal.

criteria.name: Back Angle at Bottom (~45° Inclined / Non-Vertical)
criteria.paraphrased_rule: Torso must be inclined at approximately 45 degrees relative to the horizontal floor at the bottom of the low-bar squat, maintaining spinal rigidity rather than remaining vertical.
section_and_figures: The Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong
criteria.metric_definition: Angle between the torso line (hip joint to shoulder acromion) and the horizontal floor at bottom inflection.
criteria.pass_condition_document: Approximately 45 degrees inclination to horizontal; not vertical and not collapsed flat.

app_tolerance.description: ASSUMPTION: Document states 'about 45 degrees' without upper/lower limits. Application applies a ±15° operational envelope (32° to 62°).

feedback_messages.meets_standard: Back angle is appropriately inclined (~45° to floor), preserving hamstring tension and distributing moments evenly between knees and hips.
feedback_messages.does_not_meet_standard: Back angle was too vertical (>62°) or collapsed too horizontal (<32°). Ref p. 12 notes an excessively vertical torso fails to recruit hamstrings, while collapsing horizontal indicates loss of thoracic tightness.
feedback_messages.cannot_assess: Back angle cannot be assessed: torso landmarks occluded or lifter not in side profile.

criteria.name: Bar Path Verticality & Midfoot Balance
criteria.paraphrased_rule: Barbell trajectory must travel in a straight vertical line directly over the balance point of the foot (the midfoot, halfway between heels and toes).
criteria.metric_definition: Maximum horizontal drift Delta X of the barbell center relative to the calculated midfoot axis normalized to lifter shank length.
criteria.pass_condition_document: Straight vertical line directly over the midfoot with zero unnecessary horizontal moment arm.

app_tolerance.description: ASSUMPTION: Document demands a straight vertical line. Application allows up to 16% of shank length (~3.5 cm) for natural human motor control.

feedback_messages.meets_standard: Bar path stayed vertically balanced over midfoot throughout the repetition, maximizing gravity efficiency and eliminating unwanted moment arms.
feedback_messages.does_not_meet_standard: Excessive horizontal bar drift observed relative to midfoot balance axis. Ref p. 11 notes horizontal motion creates off-balance leverage that exponentially increases effort.
feedback_messages.cannot_assess: Bar path cannot be assessed: barbell sleeve or foot sole out of frame or occluded.

criteria.name: Hip Drive Initiation out of Bottom
criteria.paraphrased_rule: Ascent out of the bottom position must be driven by shoving the hips straight upward ('butt up, not forward'); torso angle must not open/lead with the chest early.
criteria.metric_definition: Ratio of vertical hip displacement to torso inclination angle change during the initial 35% of concentric ascent.
criteria.pass_condition_document: Hips drive upward while preserving constant back inclination; lifter does not lift chest prematurely.

app_tolerance.description: ASSUMPTION: Document states 'butt up, chest stays inclined'. App operationalizes this as torso opening < 12° during initial 35% of ascent.

feedback_messages.meets_standard: Ascent was properly driven by hips: hips drove straight up out of the bottom with stable back angle, engaging the posterior chain.
feedback_messages.does_not_meet_standard: Premature chest lifting or hips shooting backward out of turnaround. Ref p. 23 explains leading with the chest slackens hamstrings and kills hip drive.
feedback_messages.cannot_assess: Hip drive cannot be assessed: turnaround frames occluded or ascent velocity tracking interrupted.

criteria.name: Knee Position at Bottom
criteria.paraphrased_rule: Knees should travel just slightly in front of toes early in descent and remain anchored in place during the bottom third rather than sliding forward late.
section_and_figures: The Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong
criteria.metric_definition: Sagittal horizontal distance between anterior patella and toe tip at bottom turnaround normalized to shank length.
criteria.pass_condition_document: Knees just a little in front of the toes, stable without late forward sliding.

app_tolerance.description: ASSUMPTION: Document states 'just a little in front of toes'. App defines ratio 0.0 to 0.45 shank length as acceptable.

feedback_messages.meets_standard: Knee position controlled: knees stay slightly in front of toes without late slide, keeping weight balanced over midfoot.
feedback_messages.does_not_meet_standard: Knees slid excessively forward past toes at the bottom, shifting excessive load onto patellar tendon and quads.
feedback_messages.cannot_assess: Knee position cannot be assessed: feet or patella landmarks occluded.

criteria.name: Eye Gaze & Cervical Spine Position
criteria.paraphrased_rule: Gaze must remain directed downward at a point on the floor 4 to 5 feet ahead with chin neutral, avoiding cervical hyperextension under barbell load.
criteria.metric_definition: Angle between head-neck line (ear-to-eye vector) and torso axis. Upward tilt indicates cervical hyperextension proxy.
criteria.pass_condition_document: Eyes focused downward 4-5 feet ahead with neck neutral; chin down.

app_tolerance.description: ASSUMPTION: Document specifies floor focus point 4-5 feet ahead; app uses head tilt angle relative to torso < 28° as an anatomical proxy (pupils cannot be directly resolved in 2D).

feedback_messages.meets_standard: Head and neck position neutral: eyes focused downward 4-5 feet ahead with chin neutral, promoting hip drive and neck safety.
feedback_messages.does_not_meet_standard: Looking up at ceiling or mirror. Ref p. 23 explains upward gaze slacks the posterior chain, pulls chest forward, and hyperextends the cervical spine under load.
feedback_messages.cannot_assess: Eye gaze cannot be assessed: facial/head landmarks occluded or lifter head out of frame.

criteria.name: Feet Flat & Heels Planted
criteria.paraphrased_rule: Heels and entire shoe sole must remain firmly planted on the floor throughout the repetition; weight must not roll forward onto toes.
criteria.metric_definition: Vertical displacement of heel keypoint relative to toe baseline at bottom turnaround.
criteria.pass_condition_document: Whole foot flat on the floor; heels firmly on the ground.

app_tolerance.description: ASSUMPTION: Zero heel lift is required by document; app permits up to 12px for shoe sole flex/tracking noise.

feedback_messages.meets_standard: Heels stayed firmly planted on the floor with weight balanced over midfoot.
feedback_messages.does_not_meet_standard: Heels lifted off the ground at the bottom. Weight shifted forward onto toes, reducing hamstring recruitment.
feedback_messages.cannot_assess: Feet or floor baseline not visible in video frame.

criteria.name: Lumbar & Thoracic Spinal Extension (Flat Back)
criteria.paraphrased_rule: The back must be held flat in rigid anatomical extension throughout the squat without lumbar flexion or rounding.
section_and_figures: The Important Things You're Going to Do Wrong
criteria.metric_definition: Deviation between hip-to-shoulder vector and intermediate spine keypoints across repetition cycle.
criteria.pass_condition_document: Normal anatomical lumbar lordosis and thoracic extension preserved; back flat.

app_tolerance.description: ASSUMPTION: 2D side view cannot reliably measure localized lumbar disc shear; severe torso collapse is flagged with uncertainty disclosure.

feedback_messages.meets_standard: Torso appeared rigid and flat without gross spinal flexion.
feedback_messages.does_not_meet_standard: Spinal flexion or rounding detected. Ref p. 19 emphasizes that a rounded back removes normal disc support and risks spinal injury.
feedback_messages.cannot_assess: Lumbar spine curvature cannot be reliably confirmed: loose clothing or plate occlusion prevents spinal curvature measurement.

criteria.name: Unrack, Walkout & Racking Safety
criteria.paraphrased_rule: The bar should be unracked with both feet under it, stepped back in a single deliberate step, locked out before descent, and returned to rack by walking forward until uprights touch.
criteria.metric_definition: Presence of single-step setup and stable lockout before first repetition descent.
criteria.pass_condition_document: 1 step back out of the rack; feet locked out before squat; walk forward to rack.

app_tolerance.description: ASSUMPTION: Assessed only if video contains unrack/walkout frames; otherwise returns CANNOT_ASSESS.

feedback_messages.meets_standard: Unrack and setup performed safely with controlled step-back and lockout.
feedback_messages.does_not_meet_standard: Unstable unrack, excessive steps taken backward, or squatted immediately without establishing balance.
feedback_messages.cannot_assess: CANNOT ASSESS: Video starts with lifter already in position or rack is outside the frame.

criteria.name: Bar Placement (Low-Bar Scapular Spine Shelf)
criteria.paraphrased_rule: Bar must rest on the shelf formed by the posterior deltoids directly below the spine of the scapula, not high on the trapezius.
criteria.metric_definition: Bar position relative to the spine of the scapula.
criteria.pass_condition_document: Bar rests directly below the spine of the scapula on posterior deltoids.

feedback_messages.cannot_assess: CANNOT ASSESS FROM SIDE VIEW: Standard 450mm Olympic bumper plates completely occlude the lifter's scapular spine and upper back in sagittal projection. Film an oblique rear-angle view to audit low-bar placement.

non_assessable_side_view_criteria.source_section: Generating hip drive & Learning to Squat
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.standard_description: Heels should be approximately shoulder-width apart. Excessively wide stance limits depth; narrow stance jams thighs against gut.
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.why_unassessable: Stance width is a coronal-plane measurement. A 2D side-view camera collapses the lateral axis. Verify by recording a frontal or rear view.

non_assessable_side_view_criteria.standard_description: Toes should point outward at approximately 30 degrees to align femurs and adductor origin/insertion angles.
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.why_unassessable: Transverse-plane rotational angle. Side-view perspective cannot resolve 30° rotation of the foot sole. Check by looking down at feet during setup.

non_assessable_side_view_criteria.criterion_name: Knees Shoved Out / Valgus Collapse Prevention
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.standard_description: Knees must be actively shoved outward to track parallel with feet, preventing medial knee valgus collapse.
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.why_unassessable: Lateral knee tracking occurs in the frontal plane. From the side, the near leg occludes the far leg and lateral knee cave is invisible. Record a front-view set to assess knee tracking.

non_assessable_side_view_criteria.criterion_name: Grip Width & Wrist Alignment (Thumbs on Top, Straight Wrists)
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.standard_description: Thumbs placed on top of bar, wrists straight with forearms to keep bar weight on back rather than loading wrists.
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.why_unassessable: Hands and wrists are occluded by 450mm bumper plates and shoulders in a 90° side view. Check grip in the rack before unracking.

non_assessable_side_view_criteria.standard_description: Bar should be racked at mid-sternum height so lifter does not have to tiptoe to unrack or rerack.
non_assessable_side_view_criteria.why_unassessable: Requires clear view of empty rack hooks relative to lifter sternum before unrack.

narrative_only_do_not_assess.topic: Front Squat vs Back Squat Mechanics Comparison
narrative_only_do_not_assess.reason_excluded: Theoretical narrative explaining why vertical front squat requires high quadriceps force. Not an evaluation standard for a barbell back squat.

narrative_only_do_not_assess.topic: Quadriceps vs Hamstrings Muscle Recruitment Claims
narrative_only_do_not_assess.reason_excluded: Anatomical/EMG narrative commentary. Muscle activation cannot be measured by computer vision without surface electromyography sensors.

narrative_only_do_not_assess.topic: Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Shearing Force Claims
narrative_only_do_not_assess.reason_excluded: Orthopedic biomechanics explanation of force cancellation. Theoretical explanation, not an assessable video rule.
Physiological description of the stretch-shortening cycle. Explains turnaround velocity, but not a pass/fail geometric rule.
